R, easiest draw circle using complex equation. unit circle, equation \(e^{\theta}\), \(e\) Euler’s number, irrational constant approximate value 2.71828; \(\) stands imaginary unit, equal \(\sqrt{-1}\); \(\theta\) refers trigonometric angle radian. make complete circle, need allow \(\theta\) take values 0 360 degrees (\(2\pi\) radian). Programmatically, need create angles ranging 0 \(2\pi\) connect make complete circle. Let us create 100 angles use circle equation (\(e^{\theta}\)). trigonometric form equation \(sin^2 \theta + cos^2 \theta = 1\), algebraic form \(x^2+y^2 = 1\). complex form, however, convenient. Unit Circle R just takes complex numbers plots values real part X axis corresponding values imaginary part Y axis. Now mark hours circle make look like clock. show 24 hours marks well marks minute marks, corresponding fraction hour. clock slightly different traditional clock 24 hours instead 12, also one hand, hour hand, minute part added hour mark fraction; second part, minor contribution, ignored. First, let us see output 24 hour marks.  time, move R package ggplot2 produce better graphics. need create R data frame plotting ggplots. also mark points minutes. First, let us create required data frame Explanation k = 24 indicates 24 hours. hour divided 4 parts , corresponding elapse successive 15 minutes. Thus, small point @ref(fig:clock24) middle two larger point (hour) means half hour elapsed. instance, point middle 7 PM 8 PM 7:30 PM. Now code exp(1i * 2 * pi * (k:1) / k) gives us angles corresponding 24 hours clock. , note angles trigonometry starts \(0^o\) (X-axis) rotates counter-clockwise, direction opposite rotation clock hands (significance difference seen shortly). clock moves clockwise. 0 degree, 3 12-hour clock 6 24-hours clock. Similarly, code SubT = exp(1i * 2 * pi * (subk:1) / subk) gives us angles corresponding fraction hour. already mentioned, clock hand rotates clock-wise, starting \(0^o\) angle, name labels 6 PM 11 PM, 12 PM 11 PM, followed 12 5 . code c(rep(" ",6), rep(" PM",12), rep(" ",6)) ensures sequence. place data two data frames subtimes dfclock, since unequal dimensions.  Next, plot lines using ggplot2 package. functions geom_path() job, geom_line() used fill gap first last point. aspect.ratio = 1 set ensure chart size depend resizing Rstudio Viewer size. points corresponding hours labelled PM using geom_text() function. need axis labels ticks. Let us remove :  completes first part plot; get skeleton clock. second final part task involves plotting event times appropriate points. Now, task several variations. simplest form, just chart, called clock_chart, plots event times 24-hour clock. optional argument Col can used change color clock hands. variations discussed later, complete discussion event times prepared plotting.
code: k <- 100 timepoint <- exp(1i * 2 * pi * (k:1) / k) plot(timepoint, pch = 19, type = "b") k <- 24 hour <- exp(1i * 2 * pi * (k:1) / k) plot(hour, pch = 19) k <- 24 # Hours subk <- 24 * 4 # Fraction of hours times <- exp(1i * 2 * pi * (k:1) / k) subtimes <- data.frame(SubT = exp(1i * 2 * pi * (subk:1) / subk)) ampm <- c(rep(" AM", 6), rep(" PM", 12), rep(" AM", 6)) library(tibble) dfclock <- tibble(   time = times,   hour = c(6:12, 1:12, 1:5), # May not be needed   label = paste0(c(6:12, 1:5), ampm) ) library(ggplot2) # Load the package ggplot2 p1 <- dfclock %>% ggplot() +   geom_path(data = subtimes, aes(Re(SubT), Im(SubT))) +   # Connect Last two missing points   geom_line(data = subtimes %>% dplyr::slice(-c(2:95)), aes(Re(SubT), Im(SubT))) +   theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +   geom_text(data = dfclock, aes(Re(time) * 1.1, Im(time) * 1.1, label = label)) +   geom_point(     data = subtimes,     aes(Re(SubT), Im(SubT)), shape = 19, color = "black", size = 0.6   ) +   geom_point(aes(Re(time), Im(time)), color = "black", size = 1.8) p1 p1 + theme(   axis.text.x = element_blank(),   axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),   axis.text.y = element_blank(),   axis.ticks.y = element_blank() ) +   labs(x = "", y = "")
